title: 大規模音声言語モデルにおける潜在的推論、効率性、およびメモリ管理の動向
titleEn: Trends in Latent Reasoning, Efficiency, and Memory Management in Large Audio Language Models
dek: 大規模音声言語モデルにおける最近の進歩は、潜在的推論、トークン効率、マルチモーダルメモリ、およびハルシネーション軽減における重要なボトルネックに対処しています。
dekEn: Recent advances in Large Audio Language Models address critical bottlenecks in latent reasoning, token efficiency, multimodal memory, and hallucination reduction.
summaryEn: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) have transformed speech and audio processing, yet they encounter severe constraints regarding computational complexity, memory scaling, and acoustic fidelity. Standard models struggle with fine-grained acoustic analysis, often expending uniform computational depth across tasks while losing nuanced information during text-aligned generation. To overcome these limitations, recent research introduces adaptive-depth latent reasoning modules, continuous thinking workspaces, and pre-transformer token pruning techniques that predict attention requirements without relying on labels. Furthermore, novel benchmarks like VoxMem evaluate multi-session conversational memory across diverse acoustic evidence types and operations, revealing distinct failure modes in long-context retention. Concurrently, multimodal direct preference optimization mitigates audio-text hallucination by enforcing acoustic grounding through perturbations. Together, these methodological innovations offer scalable pathways for deploying efficient, robust audio language systems in resource-constrained environments.
keyPointsEn: Adaptive-depth latent reasoning and continuous thinking spaces enhance fine-grained acoustic perception without inflating autoregressive generation costs.
Pre-transformer token pruning and head-aware routing strategies significantly reduce redundant audio sequences, extending context windows and GPU throughput.
Multimodal memory benchmarks and preference optimization objectives expose retention limitations and suppress audio-text hallucinations.

perspectives.label: 潜在的推論と計算効率化のメカニズム
perspectives.description: 適応深度リカレントモジュールや予測型音声トークン削減など、計算集約型のLALMにおける推論最適化メカニズムを検証します。
perspectives.labelEn: Latent Reasoning and Computational Efficiency Mechanisms
perspectives.descriptionEn: Examines inference optimization mechanisms in computationally intensive LALMs, such as adaptive-depth recurrent modules and predictive audio token reduction.

perspectives.label: 実用展開におけるコンテキストの制約と効率性
perspectives.description: 長時間の音声処理、メモリ消費、コンテキストウィンドウの制限など、実世界での展開における拡張性と効率性の課題について議論します。
perspectives.labelEn: Context Constraints and Efficiency in Practical Deployment
perspectives.descriptionEn: Discusses scalability and efficiency challenges in real-world deployment, including long-duration audio processing, memory consumption, and context window limitations.

perspectives.label: 評価ベンチマークとハルシネーション抑制
perspectives.description: マルチモーダルメモリの評価やハルシネーション軽減のための選好最適化を網羅し、モデルの信頼性と精度を測定する際の限界と課題を探ります。
perspectives.descriptionEn: Explores the limitations and challenges in measuring model reliability and accuracy, covering multimodal memory evaluation and preference optimization for hallucination reduction.

sections.heading: 音声言語モデリングにおける核心的な課題
sections.headingEn: The Core Challenges of Audio Language Modeling

blocks.text: 大規模音声言語モデルは、音声、音楽、環境音を統合されたアーキテクチャにマッピングするものの、詳細な音響分析を課されると、その動作精度が急激に低下する。従来のトランスフォーマー・アーキテクチャはすべての入力シーケンスに均一な計算深度を適用するため、単純な語彙的クエリと、話者のピッチの比較や微細な音響テクスチャの評価といった複雑な信号レベルの推論タスクとを区別することができない。さらに、標準的な音声エンコーダーによって生成される高レートのトークン・シーケンスは莫大な計算負荷を生み出し、コンテキスト・ウィンドウを急速に飽和させ、限られたハードウェア・インフラストラクチャ全体での長時間の会話展開を極めて非効率なものにする。こうしたアーキテクチャ上のボトルネックは、入力された音声と質問のペアの根底にある難易度に応じて計算資源を動的に配分できる、より洗練された推論メカニズムの緊急の必要性を浮き彫りにしている。
blocks.textEn: Large Audio Language Models map speech, music, and environmental sounds into unified architectures, yet their operational accuracy drops sharply when tasked with fine-grained acoustic analysis. Traditional transformer architectures apply uniform computational depth to every input sequence, failing to distinguish between simple lexical queries and complex signal-level reasoning tasks such as comparing speaker pitch or evaluating subtle acoustic textures. Furthermore, the high-rate token sequences generated by standard audio encoders create massive computational burdens, rapidly saturating context windows and rendering extended conversational deployment highly inefficient across limited hardware infrastructures. These architectural bottlenecks underscore the urgent necessity for more sophisticated inference mechanisms that can dynamically allocate computational resources according to the underlying difficulty of the input audio and question pair.

blocks.text: 生の計算オーバーヘッドを超えて、LALM（大規模音声言語モデル）は、永続的な音声・テキスト間の干渉やハルシネーションの傾向に頻繁に悩まされており、直接的な音響的証拠を体系的に無視する一方で、内部のテキスト事前分布に過度に依存することがよくある。音声対話ではさらに、語彙として発話された内容だけでなく、誰が話したか、パラ言語的手合図、および複数の異なる会話セッションにわたる背景の環境音までも保持できる、堅牢なマルチモーダル記憶が求められる。従来の評価フレームワークは単一セッションのコンテキスト内における表層的な語彙コンテンツに圧倒的に焦点を当てており、真の会話記憶、時間的グラウンディング、およびクロスセッションの状態追跡を測定する上で重大な評価のギャップを残してきた。その結果、研究者は、モデルが音響信号に忠実であり続けることを保証するために、包括的な評価パラダイムと選好最適化手法を確立しなければならない。
blocks.textEn: Beyond raw compute overhead, LALMs frequently suffer from persistent audio-text interference and hallucination tendencies, often over-relying on internal text priors while systematically ignoring direct acoustic evidence. Spoken interactions further demand robust multimodal memory capable of retaining not only what was said lexically, but also who spoke, paralinguistic cues, and background environmental sounds across multiple distinct conversational sessions. Prior evaluation frameworks focused predominantly on surface-level lexical content within single-session contexts, leaving critical evaluation gaps in measuring true conversational memory, temporal grounding, and cross-session state tracking. Consequently, researchers must establish comprehensive evaluation paradigms and preference optimization techniques to ensure models remain faithful to the acoustic signal.

sections.heading: 普遍的理解から効率的な推論への技術的進化
sections.headingEn: Technical Evolution from Universal Understanding to Efficient Reasoning

blocks.text: Qwen-Audioなどの初期の基礎システムは、多様な音声タイプにわたる統合されたマルチタスク学習の確立に成功し、階層的タグを通じてタスク間の干渉に対処し、予備的なマルチターン音声対話を可能にした。しかし、これらの基礎モデルは、テキスト生成のプロセスにおいて、韻律、話者の感情、周波数の詳細といった豊かな音響的詳細を体系的に破棄する、テキストにアラインされた隠れ状態に大きく依存していた。この固有の制限により、自己回帰的デコードコストを増加させることなく、本質的な音響情報を保持するように設計された特殊なアーキテクチャ拡張の開発が促され、生の音声知覚とテキスト生成の間のギャップが埋められた。
blocks.textEn: Early foundational systems such as Qwen-Audio successfully established unified multi-task training across diverse audio types, addressing cross-task interference through hierarchical tags and enabling preliminary multi-turn spoken dialogues. However, these foundational models relied heavily on text-aligned hidden states that systematically discarded rich acoustic details such as prosody, speaker affect, and frequency specifics during the text generation process. This inherent limitation spurred the development of specialized architectural extensions designed to preserve essential acoustic information without increasing autoregressive decoding costs, bridging the gap between raw audio perception and text generation.

blocks.text: 入力シーケンス長が長時間の録音に対応できるよう拡大するにつれて、研究者たちの技術的関心はトークン削減パラダイムへと移行し、従来の単純な教師なしセグメンテーションや一様な平均プーリングから、予測的プルーニング手法へとシフトしていきました。初期のトークン圧縮アプローチでは言語モデルデコーダー内部の冗長性を評価していましたが、音声トークンに対する初期の注目スコアが異常に高かったため、コストの高い言語モデル層に入る前にトークンの保持効率を最大限に高めるには、トランスフォーマー前段での予測戦略やヘッド認識型のルーティング機構の導入が不可欠となりました。
blocks.textEn: As input sequence lengths expanded to accommodate longer recordings, researchers shifted their technical focus toward token reduction paradigms, moving away from basic unsupervised segmentation and uniform average pooling toward predictive pruning methods. Early token compression approaches evaluated redundancy inside the language model decoder itself, but exceptionally high initial attention scores for audio tokens forced the adoption of pre-transformer prediction strategies and head-aware routing mechanisms to maximize token retention efficiency before entering the expensive language model layers.

sections.heading: 潜在的推論とトークン圧縮のための比較メカニズム
sections.headingEn: Comparative Mechanisms for Latent Reasoning and Token Compression

blocks.text: タスクの複雑さの変化に動的に対応するため、近年のアーキテクチャの革新では、内部での熟考を行うための特殊なモジュールが導入されています。「AdaLoop」は、学習された停止機構を備えた軽量な再帰型モジュールを導入しており、特定の音声と質問のペアに基づいて潜在的な洗練ステップを調整し、最小限のパラメータ追加で知覚集約型のサブタスクの精度を大幅に向上させます。同様に、「Continuous Audio Thinking」は、専門家の蒸留によって根拠付けられた連続的な潜在ワークスペースをモデルに備え付け、追加の自己回帰的生成オーバーヘッドを発生させることなく、単一のプリフィルステップで複雑な音響情報を整理できるようにします。これと並行して、「Triage」などのトークン圧縮技術は、エンコーダー出力からの線形予測可能性を利用して、言語モデルが実行される前に冗長な音声トークンをプルーニングし、利用可能なコンテキストウィンドウの効果的な拡大とハードウェア利用率の向上を実現します。
blocks.textEn: To address varying task complexities dynamically, recent architectural innovations introduce specialized modules for internal deliberation. AdaLoop introduces a lightweight recurrent module equipped with a learned halting mechanism that adjusts latent refinement steps based on the specific audio-question pair, adding minimal parameters while significantly boosting perception-heavy subtask accuracy. Similarly, Continuous Audio Thinking equips models with a continuous latent workspace grounded by expert distillation, allowing the model to organize complex acoustic information in a single prefill step without incurring additional autoregressive generation overhead. In parallel, token compression techniques such as Triage exploit linear predictability from encoder outputs to prune redundant audio tokens before the language model even runs, effectively expanding available context windows and improving hardware utilization.

blocks.text: 「HeadRouter」のような代替の圧縮フレームワークは、さまざまな音響ドメインにわたる個別のアテンションヘッドのスパースな寄与を活用し、リソース集約型のモデル再学習を必要とせずにトークンの重要度を動的にルーティングします。一様なダウンサンプリングや標準的なアダプターベースのファインチューニングと比較して、こうしたターゲットを絞ったルーティング戦略やトランスフォーマー前段でのプルーニング手法は、はるかに高い圧縮率を達成しつつ、下流の推論タスクに不可欠な意味的および音響的詳細を正常に保持します。したがって、実務家はこれらのプラグアンドプレイ機構を導入することで、コアモデルの忠実度を損なうことなく、多様なハードウェア構成全体でスループットを最適化できます。
blocks.textEn: Alternative compression frameworks like HeadRouter leverage the sparse contribution of distinct attention heads across various audio domains, dynamically routing token importance without requiring resource-intensive model retraining. When compared against uniform downsampling or standard adapter-based finetuning, these targeted routing strategies and pre-transformer pruning methods achieve much higher compression ratios while successfully preserving critical semantic and acoustic details for downstream inference tasks. Practitioners can thus deploy these plug-and-play mechanisms to optimize throughput across diverse hardware configurations without compromising core model fidelity.

sections.heading: 効率性、メモリ、信頼性に関する3つの視点
sections.headingEn: Tripartite Perspectives on Efficiency, Memory, and Reliability

blocks.text: 大規模音声言語モデリングに関する最新の文献を評価すると、継続的な研究開発を導く3つの補完的な視点が明らかになります。計算効率の観点からは、適応深度を持つ潜在モジュールとトランスフォーマー導入前のトークン枝刈りにより、高レートの音声シーケンスが課す重い推論負担が首尾よく軽減され、モデルがより長い入力を低遅延で処理できるようになっています。実用的なデプロイの観点からは、拡張されたマルチセッションの会話履歴を管理し、限られたハードウェアリソース全体で音声会話システムを拡張するために厳格なコンテキストバジェットを維持することが依然として極めて重要です。
blocks.textEn: Evaluating current literature in large audio language modeling reveals three complementary standpoints that guide ongoing research and development. From the computational efficiency standpoint, adaptive-depth latent modules and pre-transformer token pruning successfully alleviate the heavy inference burdens imposed by high-rate audio sequences, enabling models to process longer inputs with reduced latency. From the practical deployment perspective, managing extended multi-session conversational histories and maintaining strict context budgets remains paramount for scaling spoken conversational systems across limited hardware resources.

blocks.text: 信頼性と評価の観点からは、VoxMemやマルチモーダル直接選好最適化のような厳格なベンチマークが、テキストの事前分布のみに依存するのではなく、モデルを音響信号に直接根拠づけることの重要性を浮き彫りにしています。総合すると、これらの視点は、現代の大規模音声言語モデル（LALM）を最適化するにあたり、処理パイプライン全体を通じて、内部推論の深度、マルチセッションの記憶保持、および忠実な音響的アライメントの間の全体論的なバランスを維持する必要があることを示しています。
blocks.textEn: From the reliability and evaluation standpoint, rigorous benchmarks like VoxMem and multimodal direct preference optimization highlight the critical necessity of grounding models directly in acoustic signals rather than relying exclusively on text priors. Together, these perspectives demonstrate that optimizing modern LALMs requires maintaining a holistic balance between internal reasoning depth, multi-session memory retention, and faithful acoustic alignment throughout the entire processing pipeline.

sections.heading: 拡張シナリオにおける限界と失敗モードの評価
sections.headingEn: Evaluating Limitations and Failure Modes in Extended Scenarios

blocks.text: 大幅な構造的改善にもかかわらず、現在のモデルは、複雑な会話型記憶タスクや長文脈のシナリオで評価された際、依然として明確な制限を示しています。VoxMemなどの包括的なベンチマークを通じた実証的テストによれば、評価された大規模音声言語モデルの中で、32,000トークンといった拡張されたコンテキスト長において40%の精度を超えるものはなく、基本的な語彙内容の検索と比較して、話者の身元、パラ言語的手がかり、環境音の性能が著しく低下することが示されています。さらに、積極的なトークン圧縮バジェットは、予測の最適化にもかかわらず、重要なきめ細かい音響的詳細を時として破棄してしまうことがあり、知覚が重要となるタスクにおいて顕著な性能低下を招きます。
blocks.textEn: Despite substantial structural improvements, current models still exhibit distinct limitations when evaluated on complex conversational memory tasks and long-context scenarios. Empirical testing via comprehensive benchmarks like VoxMem indicates that no evaluated LALM exceeds forty percent accuracy at extended context lengths such as thirty-two thousand tokens, with performance degrading severely for speaker identity, paralinguistic cues, and environmental sounds compared to basic lexical content retrieval. Furthermore, aggressive token compression budgets can occasionally discard critical fine-grained acoustic details despite predictive optimizations, leading to notable performance drops in perception-heavy tasks.

blocks.text: 研究者らはまた、マルチモーダル選好最適化の目的関数が音声とテキストのハルシネーション効果的に抑制する一方で、その全体的な成功は時間的反転、周波数マスキング、ランダムノイズ注入といった特定の音響的摂動の慎重な選択に大きく依存していると指摘している。これらの実証的発見は、現行モデルが複数セッションにわたる時間的追跡や複数ターンの証拠統合において依然として大きな困難を抱えており、オープンワールドの会話型展開全体でロバストかつ長文脈な音響理解を実現する上での根本的な欠落を直接指し示していることを強調している。
blocks.textEn: Researchers also note that while multimodal preference optimization objectives effectively suppress audio-text hallucinations, their overall success depends heavily on the careful selection of specific acoustic perturbations such as temporal reversal, frequency masking, and random noise injection. These empirical findings underscore the fact that current models still struggle significantly with multi-session temporal tracking and multi-turn evidence integration, pointing directly to fundamental gaps in achieving robust, long-context acoustic understanding across open-world conversational deployments.

sections.heading: 将来の研究と実用展開に向けたインプリケーション
sections.headingEn: Implications for Future Research and Practical Deployment

blocks.text: 研究者にとって、適応型潜在推論モジュールとタスク適応型トークンプルーニングの統合は、高価なモデル全体再学習を必要とせずにベースアーキテクチャを強化する、モジュール式でプラグアンドプレイなコンポーネントを設計するための有望な新しい道を開くものである。さらに、音響的証拠とメモリ操作に関する厳密な分類体系の確立は、将来のベンチマーク開発に向けた明確な方法論的基盤を提供し、主要な研究の焦点を単なる語彙的文字起こしから、包括的なパラ言語的・複数セッション理解へとシフトさせるものである。
blocks.textEn: For researchers, the successful integration of adaptive latent reasoning modules and task-adaptive token pruning opens promising new avenues for designing modular, plug-and-play components that enhance base architectures without requiring expensive full-model retraining. Furthermore, the establishment of rigorous taxonomies for acoustic evidence and memory operations provides a clear methodological foundation for future benchmark development, shifting the primary research focus beyond simple lexical transcription toward comprehensive paralinguistic and multi-session understanding.

blocks.text: 実務家にとって、プレトランスフォーマー・トリアージやヘッドアウェア・ルーティングといった効率化手法は、単一GPU上で並行する音声ストリームを拡張し、数分に及ぶ長時間の音声記録を制約されたコンテキストウィンドウに直接適合させるための、具体的かつ実行可能なメカニズムを提供する。しかし、実務家は、知覚が重視されるタスクにおいて精度の低下につながる可能性と圧縮の度合いとのバランスを慎重に図り、配備された会話エージェントが現実世界の運用環境においてロバストな音響的基盤、低遅延、および最小限のハルシネーション率を維持できるようにしなければならない。
blocks.textEn: For practitioners, efficiency techniques such as pre-transformer Triage and head-aware routing offer concrete, actionable mechanisms to scale concurrent audio streams on single GPUs and fit extended multi-minute audio recordings directly into constrained context windows. However, practitioners must carefully balance compression aggression against potential accuracy losses in perception-heavy tasks, ensuring that deployed conversational agents maintain robust acoustic grounding, low latency, and minimal hallucination rates in real-world operational environments.

sources.title: AdaLoop: Adaptive-Depth Latent Reasoning for Audio Language Models
sources.abstract: Large audio language models answer questions about speech, sound, and music, yet their accuracy drops sharply on tasks that need fine-grained acoustic analysis. Judging which of two speakers has the higher pitch demands iterative signal-level reasoning that a content question does not. Current models spend the same computational depth on both. We introduce AdaLoop, a lightweight recurrent module that learns how many latent refinement steps a given audio--question pair requires. A shared transformer block iterates over the audio representation, guided by the question, while a learned halting mechanism exits the loop once the representation is ready. AdaLoop adds fewer than 3\% of the base model's parameters and plugs into any audio encoder--language model pair without modifying either component. Evaluated on three architecturally distinct models across MMSU, MMAU-Pro, and MMAR, AdaLoop raises the average accuracy by 2.9 to 3.8 points, with the largest gains on perception-heavy subtasks where the model learns to apply deeper reasoning.

sources.title: Hallucination Reduction for LLM-Based Audio Understanding via Multimodal Direct Preference Optimization
sources.abstract: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) are prone to hallucinating and over-relying on text priors when simultaneously presented with audio and text inputs. To mitigate these hallucinations, we propose utilizing the multimodal Direct Preference Optimization (mDPO) objective, which forces the model to ground its generation in the acoustic input by contrasting intact and distorted audio counterparts. We extend this preference learning framework to the audio domain by applying a variety of acoustic perturbations. Evaluating the Qwen2-Audio backbone across the DCASE 2025 Challenge and AH Existence datasets, we demonstrate that extending mDPO to LALMs significantly enhances temporal reasoning in the complex DCASE dataset, and improves performance on basic existence verification in the AH benchmark. We identify temporal reversal, frequency masking, and random noise as the most effective perturbations. Ultimately, our approach achieves an absolute accuracy improvement of 14.0% on the DCASE 2025 dataset and 27.4% on AH Existence.

sources.title: Audio Token Attention Is Predictable Before the Language Model Runs
sources.abstract: A large audio language model (LALM) turns a minute of speech into 750-1,500 tokens and prefills every one. Image-token pruning often cuts after the language model's first layers, where image tokens draw little attention. Audio tokens draw much more attention there, and their ranking is still far from final, so audio needs a ranking before the language model runs. Surprisingly, the attention an audio token will receive across the language model is already linearly predictable from its encoder output, before the language model runs. A linear map, fitted in closed form without labels, predicts this all-layer attention ranking at $ρ\geq .69$ on eleven of thirteen LALMs. Our method, Triage, cuts audio tokens by this prediction and, on multiple choice, cuts again at layer 2, correcting the prediction with the attention observed there. Triage sets its compression without labels, under two budgets that limit how far its output may differ from the model's own full-audio output. At the conservative budget, its word error rate and accuracy stay within .04 of full audio. At the aggressive budget, Triage beats every baseline in all twelve transcription cases. On multiple choice, at 2.2-5x compression, it outperforms DART, the strongest baseline on average, by .043 in mean accuracy. Because it cuts before the language model, it raises the audio that fits in Qwen2.5-Omni-3B's context window from 21.8 to about 62 minutes. At its most compressive point, Triage lets one GPU serve 4x as many concurrent 5-minute streams of that model. Project page: https://audio-triage.github.io

sources.title: VoxMem: Benchmarking Multimodal Memory in Large Audio Language Models
sources.abstract: Spoken conversational systems must recover information from prior interactions (i.e., memory), yet relevant information in speech extends beyond what was said to who said it, how it was spoken, and what was audible, information that exists only in the audio signal and cannot be recovered from a transcript. Beyond what to remember, memory also demands diverse operations: retrieving a single fact, integrating evidence across turns, tracking an evolving state. Real interactions further unfold across sessions, meaning information accumulates across distinct episodes rather than a single continuous recording. Existing benchmarks fall short on all three dimensions: they focus primarily on lexical content, adopt limited and ad hoc memory operations, and treat memory as a single-session problem. We argue that principled memory evaluation requires jointly characterizing the acoustic evidence to be retained and the operations applied to it, and introduce a taxonomy along these two axes. Building on this taxonomy, we present VoxMem: 3,196 evaluation instances over 34,743 spoken sessions (177 hours) crossing four acoustic evidence types (speech semantics, speaker identity, paralinguistic cues, environmental sound) with four memory operations (information extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal tracking, and answer refusal), grounded in multi-session histories and stratified across context budgets from 8K to 64K tokens. Evaluating 15 LALMs, no model exceeds 40% at 32K. Models retain what was said far better than who said it, how, or what was audible, a gap that widens for complex operations, grows with history length, and manifests as qualitatively distinct failure modes across evidence types. VoxMem aims to provide a foundation to measure and drive progress on the full scope of spoken conversational memory.

sources.title: Towards Audio Token Compression in Large Audio Language Models
sources.abstract: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) deliver strong performance across speech and audio tasks, but their audio encoders generate high-rate token sequences (e.g., 25 tokens/s), making attention computation costly and limiting scalability. In this paper, we explore techniques such as unsupervised segmentation, uniform average pooling, etc., to reduce the number of audio tokens before they are consumed by the LLM decoder. To mitigate potential performance degradation, we employ low-rank adapters during finetuning. We evaluate our proposed models on two tasks, automatic speech recognition and speech-to-speech translation tasks, that are dependent on effectively uncovering the underlying lexical content of the input signal, and study the effect of downsampling on these tasks. Experimental results show that compressed LALMs can achieve performance closer to frame-level LALMs while reducing the input audio token count up to three times before the LLM backbone.

sources.title: Qwen-Audio: Advancing Universal Audio Understanding via Unified Large-Scale Audio-Language Models
sources.abstract: Recently, instruction-following audio-language models have received broad attention for audio interaction with humans. However, the absence of pre-trained audio models capable of handling diverse audio types and tasks has hindered progress in this field. Consequently, most existing works have only been able to support a limited range of interaction capabilities. In this paper, we develop the Qwen-Audio model and address this limitation by scaling up audio-language pre-training to cover over 30 tasks and various audio types, such as human speech, natural sounds, music, and songs, to facilitate universal audio understanding abilities. However, directly co-training all tasks and datasets can lead to interference issues, as the textual labels associated with different datasets exhibit considerable variations due to differences in task focus, language, granularity of annotation, and text structure. To overcome the one-to-many interference, we carefully design a multi-task training framework by conditioning on a sequence of hierarchical tags to the decoder for encouraging knowledge sharing and avoiding interference through shared and specified tags respectively. Remarkably, Qwen-Audio achieves impressive performance across diverse benchmark tasks without requiring any task-specific fine-tuning, surpassing its counterparts. Building upon the capabilities of Qwen-Audio, we further develop Qwen-Audio-Chat, which allows for input from various audios and text inputs, enabling multi-turn dialogues and supporting various audio-central scenarios.

sources.title: Continuous Audio Thinking for Large Audio Language Models
sources.abstract: Large audio language models (LALMs) have shown impressive capabilities on diverse audio understanding tasks, ranging from speech transcription to music analysis. However, because LALMs are typically trained to produce text-aligned responses, their hidden states are progressively shaped for text generation rather than for preserving acoustic information. As a result, the diverse acoustic content that audio carries, such as phonetic detail, prosody, sound events, affect, and pitch, is lost along the way and difficult to leverage in the response. We introduce Continuous Audio Thinking (CoAT), a framework that equips audio language models with a continuous latent workspace for organizing acoustic information prior to response generation, grounded by distillation from audio experts. Within the thinking space, the model can utilize the rich acoustic information provided by expert distillation when generating its response. Furthermore, the proposed continuous thinking block can be processed in a single prefill, so CoAT does not require additional autoregressive decoding cost over the baseline. Across three LALMs, Qwen2-Audio, Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, and Audio Flamingo~3, performance gains on a broad benchmark suite spanning audio reasoning, audio understanding, music classification, speech emotion, and speech transcription demonstrate the effectiveness of CoAT. Further analysis confirms that the auxiliary supervision propagates from the thinking positions to the model's textual responses.

sources.title: HeadRouter: Dynamic Head-Weight Routing for Task-Adaptive Audio Token Pruning in Large Audio Language Models
sources.abstract: Recent large audio language models (LALMs) demonstrate remarkable capabilities in processing extended multi-modal sequences, yet incur high inference costs. Token compression is an effective method that directly reduces redundant tokens in the sequence. Existing compression methods usually assume that all attention heads in LALMs contribute equally to various audio tasks and calculate token importance by averaging scores across all heads. However, our analysis demonstrates that attention heads exhibit distinct behaviors across diverse audio domains. We further reveal that only a sparse subset of attention heads actively responds to audio, with completely different performance when handling semantic and acoustic tasks. In light of this observation, we propose HeadRouter, a head-importance-aware token pruning method that perceives the varying importance of attention heads in different audio tasks to maximize the retention of crucial tokens. HeadRouter is training-free and can be applied to various LALMs. Extensive experiments on the AudioMarathon and MMAU-Pro benchmarks demonstrate that HeadRouter achieves state-of-the-art compression performance, exceeding the baseline model even when retaining 70% of the audio tokens and achieving 101.8% and 103.0% of the vanilla average on Qwen2.5-Omni-3B and Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, respectively.
